Advances: ancora.tasks, ancora.derive, ancora.gate, ancora.parsing

Wave 1 of ancora-gg8 (D items 1-3 in the investigation record; findings-DE and the architecture decision are comments there). No contract change — performance only; every existing golden/output test must pass byte-identical. Three pure-waste fixes no prior ticket names, measured on the atlas corpus (216 subjects / 2,086 requirements):

Deliverable:
1. Prime computes the status derivation once: Prime currently calls Status.build then Next.build, and Next.build calls Status.build again internally (lib/ancora/prime.ex:12-13, lib/ancora/next.ex:20-24) — the whole derivation runs twice. Thread the built status into Next (new arity or option), saving ~10-14s recorded-scale on the worst offender.
2. Hoist resolvable_ids out of the per-decision loop: Affects.maybe_unresolved/3 rebuilds the corpus-wide id MapSet once per decision (lib/ancora/decision_parser/affects.ex:54); 260 decisions cost ~829ms per Index.build, twice in spec.check. Build once per index build, pass it in.
3. Head-only ModuleLocator for report tasks: Status passes an empty ChangeSet (lib/ancora/status.ex:31) but ModuleLocator.build always scans head AND base (lib/ancora/derive/module_locator.ex:26-31) — a byte-identical duplicate scan. Skip the base side when the change set is empty; halves the measured ~2.9s for status/next/prime.

Spec delta: none. No requirement statement changes; behavior is contract-identical. (If the Next threading forces a public API shape change, keep Next.build/1 delegating so the task surface is untouched.)

Verification:
- Tests to pass: full existing suite, byte-identical golden output tests for prime/next/status/check.
- Behaviors to demonstrate: timing evidence before/after on the ancora corpus (and the atlas corpus via --root if available): prime ≈ next after threading; index build time drop from the hoist; status ModuleLocator time roughly halved. Record numbers in the IMPLEMENTED comment.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale plus targeted files, and mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: before IMPLEMENTED, full mix test plus mix spec.check --base <stage-base>, run-until-green.
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base <stage-base> and targeted/--stale selections only; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Fixture/sandbox hygiene: async-safe fixtures, no cross-test leakage
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable/config surface
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test
- Call-site Integration: the threaded status value's production caller is Mix.Tasks.Spec.Prime via Ancora.Prime; the existing prime golden test proves the path.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/gate.ex
- lib/ancora/derive/compare.ex
- lib/ancora/derive/extract.ex
- lib/ancora/tag_scanner.ex
- lib/ancora/output*.ex

Allowed touches (this stage may modify):
- lib/ancora/prime.ex
- lib/ancora/next.ex
- lib/ancora/status.ex
- lib/ancora/decision_parser/affects.ex
- lib/ancora/derive/module_locator.ex (empty-changeset skip only)
- lib/ancora/index.ex (only if the resolvable_ids hoist needs a pass-through)
- test/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.parsing.spec.md (substantive statements describing the single-derivation, head-only-locator, and hoisted-resolvable-ids changes, plus the decisions: frontmatter link; orchestrator ruling 2026-09-03T23:00Z — the original "Spec delta: none" was wrong)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No parallelization (that is the wave-2 parallel-parsing ticket, sequenced after ancora-xla.3)
- No caching of any kind, in-memory-across-runs or on-disk (ancora-u38 is deferred by ruling)
- No output or flag changes; goldens must not change
- Do not touch anything in ancora-xla.3's scope (gate.ex materialize, compare.ex, extract.ex)

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

The ticket's Allowed touches exclude all four files, and its Advances field names only ancora.tasks. The worker contract forbids reading the other three subjects or making out-of-scope edits without an orchestrator ruling. No second final-tier run was attempted.

RULING: describe the real change in the four subject specs; remove the growth; no drift trailer

The ticket's "Spec delta: none" was wrong: ancora's drift rule fires when a function a subject's tests reach changes body, and clears only when that subject's spec moves with it. The honest clear here is a short, true statement per subject, not silence. Scope is widened accordingly:

1. Advances: now reads `ancora.tasks, ancora.derive, ancora.gate, ancora.parsing`. Read those four subjects (and only those).
2. Allowed touches now include `.spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md`, `.spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md`, `.spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md`, `.spec/specs/ancora.parsing.spec.md`. In each, make a substantive requirement or scenario edit that states what actually changed and is observable: tasks — prime builds the status derivation once and next reuses it; derive — the module locator skips the base scan when the change set is empty; parsing — affects validation resolves against one resolvable-id set built once per index build; gate — the index the gate builds resolves affects against that single set. Tag a test to each new or amended statement where one already pins it (your locator, prime, and affects tests qualify). No padding: one or two sentences each.
3. Growth: eliminate it. Do not introduce a new public arity that tests call directly. Thread the built status through an option on the existing Next.build arity, or a private function, so Next.build/1 stays the only task surface (the ticket already asked for this). If a new public binding is truly unavoidable, describe it in ancora.tasks.spec.md and say why in the completion record.
4. Do NOT add `Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info` or `derived/growth=info`; a code-keyed downgrade over the epic range would blind the merge gate to real drift in sibling tickets. The only trailer authorized on this epic is `Spec-Ack: change/missing_decision=info`, which your spec edits will now need: add `ancora.decision.field_friction_response` to each edited spec's `decisions:` frontmatter list (its affects: names all four subjects) and put that one trailer on the commit with a body line naming the ADR.
5. Your red final-tier run 1 does not count against the cap: it was red solely on findings the ticket contract did not anticipate. Two capped runs remain. Goldens for prime/next/status/check must still be byte-identical; that part of the contract is unchanged.
Then record IMPLEMENTED with the same session tag (gg8.4-impl-1) and log path. No child ticket is carved; this consumes no attempt.

TEST_CRITIC: PASS
Session: e92f6de6-94f7-4814-8140-19f3f3007d0a
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-remembers/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/e92f6de6-94f7-4814-8140-19f3f3007d0a.jsonl

Read-only review of test/ancora/next_test.exs and test/ancora/derive/module_locator_test.exs at 0ce4e80 against the ticket contract (goldens byte-identical, derivations not duplicated), the RULING widening to four subject specs, and the four spec edits. The four touched test files run green (18 tests, 0 failures). No material defect: the one dedupe that is observable through a public API (Next reusing a supplied status) has a discriminating test, and the goldens that carry the contract are untouched and passing. Two warnings and one observation follow.

What holds up

- next_test.exs:24-35 is a real discriminator. It uses the same fixture as the test at line 11, which yields classification "covered local change" when Next builds status itself. Passing status: %{subjects: []} flips the classification to "uncovered frontier change". If Next ignored the option and called Status.build anyway, line 33 fails. The comment on line 25 is accurate.
- The standalone half of the amended ancora.tasks.prime_loop statement ("standalone Next runs shall build their own status") is pinned by the four pre-existing Next tests that pass no status option.
- module_locator_test.exs:39-57 protects the skip guard from being too eager: it builds a ChangeSet with entries: [] (struct default) but non-empty prefetched, and asserts base and head differ. A revert of the map_size(prefetched) == 0 guard to an entries-only check would fail here. Both clauses of the new scan_base_sources/3 are exercised.
- Fixture hygiene is fine: @moduletag :tmp_dir, per-test git repos, no shared state, async-safe.

Warning 1: module_locator_test.exs:35 cannot fail on a revert of the change it was added for

assert locator.base == locator.head is true on the pre-change code too. With an empty change set, base_sources/3 (module_locator.ex:72-95) maps every head path to :unchanged and returns exactly head_sources, and scan_sources/2 is deterministic, so the old two-scan code produced an equal map. The assertion therefore pins "base equals head" (which was always true) but not "HEAD is scanned once", which is the clause the amended ancora.derive.membership_source_derived statement adds. It would fail if the new clause returned garbage; it would not fail if someone reverted scan_base_sources to a second scan_sources call. The IMPLEMENTED record's "pin identical head/base maps" is literally accurate but is weaker than "pins the skip". If a failing-capable pin is wanted, :erts_debug.same(locator.base, locator.head) asserts term identity and does fail on a fresh rebuild; that is a hack and I would accept the current equality plus the recorded timing evidence instead. Not a contract defect: the failure it lets through is a perf regression, and the ticket verifies perf by timing evidence, not by test.

Warning 2: the Prime half of the amended ancora.tasks.prime_loop statement has no test that can fail

"Prime shall build the status derivation once and pass that report to Next" is pinned only by prime_test.exs:11, whose assertions on report.lines are byte-identical whether Prime threads the status or not. The new Next test proves Next honors the option but is tagged ancora.tasks.next_labels_verbatim, which is honest for its label assertions but leaves prime_loop's new sentence without a discriminating test. Prime.build/2 has no public seam that exposes whether Status.build ran once or twice, so this is inherent to a perf-only change. Suggest dual-tagging the new Next test with ancora.tasks.prime_loop so the amended sentence at least links to the test that proves the reuse mechanism it depends on. Same category as Warning 1: the failure let through is a silent return to double derivation, not a golden change.

Observation for the auditor: Affects.validate/2 map clause now has test-only callers

lib/ancora/decision_parser/affects.ex keeps a validate(decision, current_index) clause that builds the id set on the fly. Production (Index.build via DecisionParser.validate_affects) now always passes a MapSet, so that clause is reached only from decision_parser_test.exs:205, 222, and 249. The tests still exercise the MapSet clause transitively, so the hoisted path is covered, and the amended ancora.parsing.adr_grammar and ancora.gate.strict_verdict sentences ("build once per index build") are, like the two warnings above, not pinned by any test that could fail on a revert. Flagging because the ticket's standing bounce class asks for a production call site per callable surface; this is a retained clause, not a new one, so I leave the call to the auditor.

Tag honesty: next_labels_verbatim on the new Next test is honest (it asserts the two labels verbatim). membership_source_derived on the extended locator test is honest for lines 31-34 and literally true for line 35. Nothing asserted is tautological in the sense of comparing a value with itself; line 35 is tautological only relative to the change under test, as described in Warning 1.

Verdict: PASS

Notes:
- None of the three "once" statements has a test that distinguishes new code from old. The added `assert locator.base == locator.head` also passes on the base SHA: with an empty prefetched map, base_sources equals head_sources, so the old double scan produced equal maps. The skip is provably identity-preserving for the same reason. Dedupe is proven by reading plus the implementer's timings, which is what the ticket asked for; a discriminating test would need an instrumentation seam the ticket does not authorize.
- Timing method is thin: "paired ... averaged" gives no run count, harness, or how the legacy path was reconstructed, and "180 decisions" is not the ancora corpus (6 decisions), so a synthetic fixture was used without being named.
- ancora.decision.field_friction_response affects: lists findings, gate, derive, tasks, scaffold but not ancora.parsing. The ruling's premise "its affects: names all four subjects" is false for parsing. No gate effect today because the trailer clears missing_decision, but once the ADR-based suppression lands, parsing's decisions: link will not resolve back. Fix belongs on the ADR, outside this ticket's Allowed touches.
- The new Next test tags next_labels_verbatim rather than the amended prime_loop statement. Advisory; prime_loop already has two pinning tests.
- spec.next rejects --root while spec.status/prime/check accept it. Pre-existing, unrelated to this diff.
